m1-red-regression.title: TDD red: add the reviewer's own regression case to tests/test_context_determinism.py, BEFORE touching production code
m1-red-regression.imperative: Add a new test method to tests/test_context_determinism.py's RealCheckoutSkew class (or a clearly-related sibling method there) reproducing the reviewer's exact BLOCKER-1 case: two FRESH git worktrees at the SAME commit, NOTHING overlaid; one stays genuinely clean, the other gets a one-line appended edit to docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md (a file NO context_refs declaration names -- reuse the reviewer's own choice of file). The declaration must name only tracked, unmodified files (reuse RealCheckoutSkew.TRACKED) so declared canon is byte-identical on both sides. Establish the premise with real git status output (one side's --porcelain is empty, the other's is not) before asserting. THE regression assertion is `self.assertEqual(cm.content(m_clean), cm.content(m_dirty))` -- do not additionally assert which subtree `dirty` lives in inside this same test method (that would crash with KeyError against the CURRENT pre-fix shape, where `run` has no `dirty` key yet); keep the shared assertions safe to run unchanged both before and after the fix, so the SAME test text produces the red and the green transcript. Run it now, before any production-code edit this round, and confirm it FAILS (content differs -- pre-fix `repo_rev` carries `dirty` inside content). Paste the failing pytest transcript into IMPLEMENTER_RESULT-rework1.md verbatim. Do not weaken or delete any existing test in this file. Attest c1 (manual: red observed) -- do NOT use a command check here, it would run the by-design-failing test and block this gate.

m2-split-fix.title: The surgical split: commit stays content, dirty moves to /run
m2-split-fix.imperative: Implement REWORK-1.md's split. In scripts/context_manifest.py: CONTENT_KEYS stays (contract, step, files, repo_rev) but `repo_rev` in the manifest now carries `{commit}` only; `run_facts()` gains a `dirty` parameter and the `run` subtree carries `run.dirty`; `build_manifest()` calls `repo_state(roots)` once, splits the returned {commit, dirty} pair at assembly (repo_revision()/default_repo_state() themselves keep returning both -- the split is NOT pushed into the git helper). Update the module docstring's point 1, the CONTENT_KEYS comment, and default_repo_state()'s docstring to describe the split and why it does not reopen the honesty gap (content already carries the per-file blob OID as the precise per-byte answer; repo_rev.commit only has to be the coarse traceability stamp). In scripts/checklist_engine.py, rewrite repo_revision()'s docstring: remove the disproven claim that `dirty` keeps the repo-wide SHA honest INSIDE content, replace with the corrected argument from REWORK-1.md (commit is canon-determined so it is safe as content; dirty is a fact about the producing working tree, not the delivered bytes, so it belongs in /run; the per-file rev already answers the honesty question dirty was protecting). Update docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md's 'Two-level revision scheme' paragraph to match. Update the existing tests/test_context_manifest.py::RepoRevContent class (every test currently asserting `m['repo_rev'] == {commit, dirty}` or `m['repo_rev']['dirty']`) to the new split shape, and add a new test asserting content is byte-identical for two repo_state fakes that share `commit` but differ on `dirty` (in-process, fast complement to the git-worktree regression). Do NOT touch rev(), the per-file row shape, or docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md. Attest c1 (test-after/inspection for this wiring-level change, matching the original gate's test mode) and satisfy c2/c3/c4 (commands) -- c4 is the m1 regression test, now expected GREEN; paste the passing transcript into IMPLEMENTER_RESULT-rework1.md beside the m1 failing one.

m3-major2-comment.title: MAJOR-2: correct the AST guard's comment, add the injectability test it should have had
m3-major2-comment.imperative: In tests/test_context_manifest.py::ProducerGuards::test_producer_shells_out_to_nothing, the comment above `banned = {...}` currently claims 'no git process ... at assembly time. The manifest is a pure function of (canon, selector)' -- false since build_manifest shells out via the default repo_state edge. Re-comment it to state the guard's actual, narrower property: this file's own source contains none of these identifiers at the AST level; it does NOT mean build_manifest never shells out (the default repo_state edge delegates to checklist_engine.repo_revision, which does, by design, so context_manifest.py's own no-subprocess guarantee stays true after repo_rev exists). Add a new test in the same class asserting the invariant that actually matters: with BOTH `reader` and `repo_state` injected as fakes, build_manifest performs zero subprocess calls (patch subprocess.run/Popen to raise if called, mirroring the existing filesystem-enumeration guard pattern in test_no_globs_or_filesystem_enumeration_anywhere_in_the_producer). Attest c1 and satisfy c2.
